machine.name: Apple M5 Pro
machine.reference: official BLAKE3 1.8.7: b3sum and the blake3 crate with NEON + rayon

status_note: Numbers from 2026-10-26; NVIDIA results are pending: Bend 2.0.39's CUDA runtime hangs inside Modal's sandbox.

in_memory.note: Warm, data already in memory, same bytes and same digest. Rust = blake3 crate (NEON + rayon).

cli.note: One-shot `b3sum FILE...` (process start included), medians of 15 interleaved rounds; output byte-identical to the official b3sum.

daemon.note: A long-running process, start-up excluded: every round re-opens and re-reads the files and hashes them. Rust seq = one file at a time, as b3sum; Rust par = rayon across files (the strongest baseline). Bend GPU reads into reused blocks of a 4 GB Metal heap set up once, then hashes every file in one bang. Medians of 21 rounds on a busy machine (load average ~20).

iroh.note: iroh-blobs 0.103 ingest (add_path: BLAKE3 + bao outboard, plus the store's own bookkeeping) into a fresh store, against Bend computing the same hash and the same outboard (byte-identical to bao-tree's) in a long-running process. Best of 5 rounds each.

floors: Page faults on a mapped file: ~15 ms per GiB, serialized in the kernel (shared by every tool).
All-core CPU ceiling near 38 GB/s for BLAKE3 on this chip (Rust and Bend both reach it).
macOS open(): ~48 ms per 10,000 files at best, however many threads (volume-wide serialization).
GPU start-up: the Metal heap costs ~50 ms per GiB to set up, so one-shot CLI runs stay on the CPU.

Uncached files: the SSD reads 10-14 GB/s with large parallel preads but 0.2-0.8 GB/s through page faults, so mapping a file that is not in the page cache throws most of the SSD away (Bend streams those).
NVIDIA GPUs: Bend 2.0.39's CUDA runtime hangs inside Modal's sandbox, even for the guide's pow2! example, while plain CUDA managed memory works there; NVIDIA numbers wait on that.

techniques.title: BLAKE3 core in Bend2
techniques.summary: Unboxed U32 records compile to register code; Array<U32> is a packed buffer; Array.fork shares input down a parallel fork tree.

techniques.title: 8-lane compress8 + clang SLP
techniques.summary: Eight chunks per call, word-major lanes, one call site, SLP and inline flags: 2.95 GB/s per core vs NEON's 2.40.

techniques.title: b3sum I/O path
techniques.summary: Parallel one-pass loader, zero-copy read-only mmap, byte-balanced file tree, one write for all output.

techniques.title: Files past 4 GiB
techniques.summary: 1 GiB segments are complete BLAKE3 subtrees, hashed in parallel and merged as parents; up to 4 TiB.

techniques.title: Flat GPU leaves
techniques.summary: Fork-free 4/16/64-chunk leaves sized to the 16,384-lane cube: 93-110 GB/s on the GPU.

techniques.title: Daemon race, map zone, iroh outboards
techniques.summary: Mapped files go into an address-space zone of their own (one munmap a round); the CPU tree also emits iroh-blobs' bao outboard, byte-identical to bao-tree.

techniques.title: Streaming and a GPU daemon
techniques.summary: Files not in the page cache stream in 1 GiB segments with 16 F_NOCACHE readers while Bend hashes (101.5 GB in ~7.6 s); a daemon refills reused GPU-heap blocks and hashes in one bang.

models.note: Real model weights from deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (MIT), one-shot b3sum FILE... on a 64 GB Mac, identical hashes. Files this size are mostly not in the page cache: the official b3sum reads them through page faults (16 KiB at a time); Bend checks residency and streams them in 1 GiB segments with large parallel preads while it hashes. The official b3sum took 526 s on its first run of the 101.5 GB shard.

rows.workload: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash shard 48 (101.5 GB, bigger than RAM)
